player.name: Kren Brook
player.concept: A jaded ex-military type who's mostly looking for the shortest somplest path to sort things out.

established: Sewn into the lining of Prout's left boot was a page razored from the Royal Granary Roll: a dozen grain wagons for the King's Road this past month marked 'lost to goblins', each countersigned 'J. Sallow, for the Royal Purveyor', with Prout's pencilled note beside each of what the same wagon weighed at the river warehouses two days later, and at the foot: 'Not goblins. Who pays the hedge-folk?'
canon: Cob claims the oversized boots are his and says he found them.
Kell has offered to record that Cob is wearing Prout's boots.
notes: Keep Cob’s fear of the loft distinct from his pride about throwing. If Kren gets Prout close enough to examine, give the prepared physical evidence and let Kell record what she can swear to.

transition.when: Kren gets Prout down or otherwise close enough to examine his neck, head, or hands.

check.reason: to examine Prout for signs he was killed before he was hanged
check.success: You find evidence that Prout was struck and strangled before he was hoisted; Kell records the findings.
check.failure: You cannot read the marks clearly enough to tell how he died; Kell records that the examination was inconclusive.

patches.why: The body examination can supply the missing evidence that Prout did not die by his own hand.

repairs.assessment: Kren is taking the direct route through Kell’s knowledge, and her regret gives the case a personal stake without yet proving murder. The scene is moving well; leave the next investigative choice with Kren.
repairs.notes: Kell has told this once; don't have her repeat it. Her account and the barred loft are leads, not yet a proved homicide—support Kren’s next reasonable move without deciding it for them.

repairs.assessment: Kren is looking for the shortest practical way to examine the body. The scene is moving forward: the barred loft door already gives a concrete reason to doubt suicide.
repairs.notes: The suicide story is broken; move the tracker to doubt. Don’t conjure a ladder: the loose board behind the water butt is a plausible way into the loft, and Cob might give it away with one involuntary glance if Kren looks for access. From inside, they can untie the hoist and lower Prout; Kell can hold the line and examine him once he’s down.

repairs.assessment: Kren is pursuing the suspicious boot after noticing Cob’s tell; the scene is moving naturally toward the evidence. Keep the focus on what Kren does with Cob’s claim rather than having another character explain the clue for him.
repairs.notes: Let Cob resist anyone taking the boots, but allow a fair bargain or respectful request to get a real response; don't make Kren roll just to inspect them if Cob agrees. If the left boot is examined, the crackling stiff lining can lead to the page.

repairs.assessment: Kren is pursuing the evidence in a practical, direct way, and the page has opened the motive and named Sallow. The scene is on track; the page alone does not yet establish who was in the loft or prove how Prout died.
repairs.notes: Give Kren a moment to put together what the page proves. Don’t let the page alone settle that Prout was murdered or that Sallow was present; Cob’s account and the body remain live avenues.

repairs.assessment: Kren has found the page and is pursuing the body examination, while using a playful military connection to engage Cob. The scene is on track; let the javelin moment breathe without making it a substitute for Cob’s trust or the loft access.
repairs.notes: Keep Cob’s fear of the loft distinct from his pride about throwing. If Kren gets Prout close enough to examine, give the prepared physical evidence and let Kell record what she can swear to.

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Prout turns slowly on the hoist rope above the shut loft door. A pigeon sits on the beam, regarding the proceedings with professional detachment. Below, a scrawny boy in enormous black boots lobs gutter stones at the body. “Spin, you miserable sack of bones!” On the wall, a sharp-faced girl swears at him, the yard, and the weather in Common and something that sounds like dockside Saltmere.

A woman in a rain cape steps away from the gate, notebook open. “Sergeant Kell. The Captain says suicide. I haven’t written that down.” Her gaze stays on your hands. A stone clangs off the hoist hook.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: Hello there. Sergent Agnes I assume? Apparently i'm needed again.

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Sergeant Kell gives you a measured look. “Sergeant Agnes Kell. You’re Kren Brook, then. The King’s investigator.” Her pencil rests over the open notebook. “Needed is a generous word. Lent, I think.”

The boy in the too-big boots sends another stone at the corpse. “Cob don’t care who’s needed. Bluebottles come, bluebottles go.” He glances at Kell’s notebook, then at you. “That one’s got a list, probably.”

The girl on the wall snorts. “And a face like a wet boot. Careful, Cob.”

Kell turns a page with her thumb. “The Captain calls it suicide. I haven’t written that down.”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: Any reason to suspect otherwise?

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Kell glances up at Prout. “There are reasons to look. Not yet reasons to call it murder.”

She taps her pencil once against the notebook. “The loft door is barred from the inside. The rope runs through the wall and is tied off up there. The porters found him at first light; the yard doors were padlocked when they arrived.” Her eyes settle on the body again. “And the Captain decided before anyone examined him.”

Cob’s next stone strikes the wall short. The girl in the shawl watches you, chin lifted. “I saw him jump,” she says. “Moonlight, midnight, wailing about his debts. Clear as day.” Kell’s pencil pauses over the page.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: Did you know the man Kell?

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Kell’s pencil stills. For a moment she watches the body turning above the shut loft door.

“I knew him by sight,” she says. “He said good morning to the watch. Not many do.”

She looks back at you. “Three days ago, he came to the watch house asking how a clerk reports false entries in the King’s rolls.” Her voice stays level; her thumb presses hard against the notebook’s edge. “He asked whether we could arrest a gentleman of the Purveyor’s office. I told him to take it to the palace.”

The pencil touches paper. “I should have listened.”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: Oh? *my face draws to a point* False entries? You suspect corruption?

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Kell’s gaze holds on you a beat. “I suspect he believed there were false entries. I don’t know whether he was right.”

Her pencil moves, then stops. “The Purveyor’s office has its own people and its own doors. The watch does not go through them on a clerk’s question.” A faint crease appears beside her mouth. “That is what I told him.”

Across the yard, the girl’s fist tightens around something small and bright. Cob’s stones stop for half a breath, then resume their patient assault on the dead. Kell watches you. “What do you want examined, investigator?”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: You think these two saw anything?

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Kell looks from the boy throwing stones to the girl on the wall. “They were here when the porters found him. The boy says he’s throwing stones because it makes Prout spin. The girl says she saw him jump.”

The girl’s chin lifts. “I did.”

Kell’s pencil rests above the page. “That is what they say, investigator. Whether they saw anything else is another matter.” Cob stops throwing for a moment, watching you with his fists full of stones.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: Right well can we get the body down and investigate?

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Kell looks up at the body. “We can. The rope is tied off inside the loft, and the door is barred from the inside. The porters’ ladders are locked in the granary; the warden has the key, and she’s at the palace.”

She glances over the swept-bare cobbles. “The dead-cart brings a ladder at noon. Before then, we need a way up—or into the loft.” Cob’s stones fall silent. The girl on the wall watches you, her fist closed around something.

Kell taps her pencil against the notebook. “What do you have in mind, investigator?”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: If he was murdured then hung up to make it look like a suicide, we might be able to see other wounds.

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Kell follows your gaze up to Prout. “Yes. From the ground, we can’t tell whether there are other wounds beneath his clothes.”

She shuts the notebook. “The loft door is barred from inside, and the rope is tied off up there. If we reach the loft, we can lower him and I’ll examine him.”

Cob shifts in the oversized boots. One heel crackles. His eyes flick, quick as a stone, toward the water butt; the girl on the wall catches it and goes very still. Kell notices the exchange but says nothing.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: What's the matter with you two? Very tense all of a sudden?

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
The girl’s fist closes tighter. “Tense? We’re standing under a dead man, with a watch sergeant writing down whatever people say. What’s to relax about?”

Cob shifts his weight. The oversized left boot gives a dry crackle. His eyes dart toward the water butt, then back to you. “Cob’s fine. Cob’s always fine.”

Kell watches him, then the girl. She doesn’t move to block either of them. “They’ve both had a long morning, investigator.” Her pencil touches the notebook. “That’s what I can put down.”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: what's crackling in your boot boy?

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Cob’s chin lifts. “Boot’s got a boot thing in it. None of your business.”

The left heel crackles again as he shifts. He looks down at it, then quickly back at you, fists tight around the stones. The girl on the wall leans forward. “Leave him be.”

Kell stays still, notebook open. “I’ll note that the boy is wearing the deceased’s boots, if you want it recorded, investigator.” Cob’s eyes flick to the page, wary. “They’re mine,” he says, quieter. “Found ’em.”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I'm not sure he's going to miss them. You can have them for all I'm concerned, though they're a little big for you. If you'd let me, I'd like to investigate them though. Sounds like something crackling in the left boot.

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Cob looks from you to the girl in the shawl. “You said I can keep ’em?”

“Yes,” you’ve made clear; he studies your face, suspicious of any grown-up sentence that sounds too simple. Then he gives a short, reluctant nod. “Look, then. Don’t nick ’em.”

Kell’s pencil hovers. “Boots: the deceased’s. The boy may keep them. Investigator to examine the left boot.” She writes it down.

The girl’s shoulders ease only slightly as Cob lifts his left foot. The heel gives a dry crackle when he sets it down. “There,” he says. “Boot thing.”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I inspect the boot

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Cob plants his foot carefully. The oversized left boot crackles beneath your hands. Pressing along the stiff heel, you find a ridge under the lining; a few stitches have been worked there, neat and tight.

“Don’t cut it,” Cob says, suddenly small. “They’re mine.”

Kell watches without moving. The girl on the wall has gone quiet, her eyes fixed on the boot. The hidden thing shifts faintly beneath the leather when you touch it.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I just want to see what's been stitched inside here. I'll be careful.

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Cob holds his foot steady, watching your hands. “Careful, then.”

The stitches are small and tight. You work them apart without tearing the leather; a folded strip of paper slides into your palm. Cob stares at it, then at the boot. “That was in there?”

Kell steps closer, notebook ready. The paper is creased and inked on both sides. Among the ruled entries you can make out wagons marked “lost to goblins,” each countersigned: “J. Sallow, for the Royal Purveyor.”

Kell’s pencil touches the page. “Noted. A page from the Royal Granary Roll, found sewn into the deceased’s boot.”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: Thank you Cob. You've been very helpful.

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
“Thank you, Cob. You’ve been very helpful.”

Cob scowls at you, but doesn’t take back his foot. “Cob was helpful because Cob allowed it. Boots stay with Cob.”

Kell has gone very still over the page. “Those entries are countersigned by J. Sallow.” Her pencil moves across the notebook. “Prout came to me three days ago about false entries in the King’s rolls. I sent him to the palace.” She swallows once, then reads as she writes: “A page removed from the Royal Granary Roll, found sewn into the deceased’s boot. Wagons recorded lost to goblins; countersigned J. Sallow, for the Royal Purveyor.”

The girl on the wall has gone pale. Kell looks up. “That establishes the entries. On what evidence was Prout murdered?”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I suppose we need to inspect the body. You said we could get up there somehow?

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Kell looks up at the body. “There is a way into the loft. The boy may know it.”

Cob’s shoulders tense. The girl in the shawl snaps, “Don’t you start.”

Kell keeps her voice even. “A loose board behind the water butt. Child-sized. A grown person might squeeze through, but I’m not climbing after you.” She glances at the boy’s oversized boots, then back to you. “If we get inside, we can lower Prout from the loft. I’ll examine him there.”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: Say Cob, you're a deft shot. Ever thrown a javlin before?

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Cob eyes the javelin, then you. His swagger returns by inches. “Cob’s thrown stones. Good ones, too. Javelins are for soldiers and people with more arm than sense.”

Moll gives a sharp laugh from the wall. “He’ll throw anything if there’s a chance of hitting you with it.”

Kell turns her notebook slightly, keeping the page safe from the damp. “The board behind the water butt is still our way in, investigator.” Cob’s gaze flicks from your weapon to the little opening, and the bravado thins again. “Cob’s not squeezing in there for anybody.”

hanged-clerk:place.name: The yard behind the King's Granary
hanged-clerk:place.description: A cobbled yard behind the granary, swept bare for the Assembly, smelling of wet grain, pigeons and river mud. Over the wall the city is hanging bunting.

lane.name: the lane
lane.description: The lane beyond the yard wall, with an old elm leaning over it.

yard.name: the yard
yard.description: Cobbles, a water butt, the padlocked yard doors and, on the granary's back wall, the hoist.

loft.name: the tally loft (above the yard, inside the granary)
loft.description: Up under the granary roof: the tally desk, grain stacks, Cob's nest. Reached by the loft door (barred inside) or Cob's loose board behind the water butt.

notes.text: just inside the gate, notebook out
Was here when the porters found Prout; says he throws stones to make Prout spin.
Seems tense; says he is fine.
sitting on top of the yard wall
Was here when the porters found Prout; says she saw him jump.
Tense and defensive about being questioned beneath Prout's body.

elm.name: the old elm
elm.description: Old, dry and leaning over the wall into the yard; pigeons in it.

satchel.name: Prout's satchel
satchel.description: Lying open and empty by the gate.

hoist-beam.name: the hoist beam
hoist-beam.description: Juts out high above the loft door, with a pulley; the rope runs up over it and in through a slot to a cleat inside.

hoist-rope.name: the hoist rope

notes.text: Runs through the wall and is tied off in the loft.

hoist-rope.description: Runs over the pulley and in through the slot above the loft door; the noose end holds Prout well out of reach of the cobbles.

prout.name: Wendell Prout's body
prout.description: A small grey-coated clerk with ink-stained fingers, in darned stockings, no boots; a swelling at the back of the skull, a level cord mark under the noose burn, clean palms.

loft-door.name: the loft door
loft-door.description: High in the wall under the hoist beam; barred on the inside.

yard-doors.name: the granary's yard doors
yard-doors.description: Big double doors, padlocked; the warden has the key, at the palace.

loose-board.name: a loose board behind the water butt

notes.text: A child-sized way into the loft; a grown person might squeeze through.

loose-board.description: Cob's way into the loft: child-sized; a grown-up could squeeze through with effort.

cleat.name: the rope cleat
cleat.description: Inside the loft door: the hoist rope tied off on it with a docker's knot.

tally-desk.name: the tally desk
tally-desk.description: Ink spilled across it, a smashed lantern beside it, heel scuffs in the grain dust from here to the loft door.

granary-roll.name: the Royal Granary Roll
granary-roll.description: The big book, chained to the desk, with a page razored out. The pages either side list King's Road grain wagons 'lost to goblins', each countersigned 'J. Sallow, for the Royal Purveyor'.

cobs-nest.name: a nest of sacking in the loft
cobs-nest.description: Sacks and candle-ends behind the grain stacks: Cob's castle.

boots.name: Prout's good black boots

notes.text: Cob permits the player to examine the boots, but not to take them; the left heel crackles when he sets it down.

boots.description: Three sizes too big for Cob, laced on with string; the backs of both heels scraped raw, and the left one crackles when he stamps.

ledger-page.name: a folded page sewn into the left boot's lining

notes.text: A folded strip from the Royal Granary Roll, with entries for wagons marked “lost to goblins,” countersigned “J. Sallow, for the Royal Purveyor.”

ledger-page.description: A page razored from the Royal Granary Roll: wagons 'lost to goblins', countersigned 'J. Sallow, for the Royal Purveyor', with Prout's pencilled river-warehouse weights and 'Not goblins. Who pays the hedge-folk?'

wheat-crown.name: a silver crown stamped with a wheat-ear
wheat-crown.description: What the gentleman paid her to say she saw the clerk jump.

silver-crowns.name: silver crowns
silver-crowns.description: Heavy silver with the King's face, a little worn.

pennies.name: pennies
pennies.description: Copper, twelve to the shilling, and the currency of the Drowned Rat.

log.text: Kren Brook now has 2 silver crowns
note on the hoist rope: Runs through the wall and is tied off in the loft.
note on Cob: Was here when the porters found Prout; says he throws stones to make Prout spin.
note on Moll: Was here when the porters found Prout; says she saw him jump.
note on Cob: His stones have fallen silent.
note on Moll: Tense and defensive about being questioned beneath Prout's body.
note on Cob: Seems tense; says he is fine.
note on Prout's good black boots: Cob permits the player to examine the boots, but not to take them; the left heel crackles when he sets it down.
note on Prout's good black boots: A neat, tight line of stitches hides a ridge beneath the lining at the stiff heel; something inside shifts faintly when touched.

note on a folded page sewn into the left boot's lining: A folded strip from the Royal Granary Roll, with entries for wagons marked “lost to goblins,” countersigned “J. Sallow, for the Royal Purveyor.”
note on a loose board behind the water butt: A child-sized way into the loft; a grown person might squeeze through.

opened.title: Cob claims the boots are his

whispers.note: He likes being taken seriously as a good shot, but the loft still scares him; he wants to keep the boots and stay out of the hole.
She wants Cob kept away from the loft and the watch, and is ready to snap if Kren pushes him into danger.
She wants Prout examined before the evidence is lost, but won’t claim murder without something she can put in her notebook.
